overview: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals adjudicates petitions for variances, special permits, and Chapter 40B comprehensive permits for residential and commercial developments. Meeting from late 2023 through late 2026, the board has managed significant growth in high-density housing while addressing individual property hardships such as flooding and topographical constraints. Its work frequently involves reconciling large-scale multifamily projects with neighborhood concerns regarding traffic, massing, and infrastructure. As of September 2026, the board is focused on interpreting updated state guidelines regarding accessory dwelling units and the conversion of non-conforming commercial spaces into residential uses.

threads.name: Chapter 40B Comprehensive Permits
threads.summary: The board spent much of 2024 conducting an intensive review of a 289-unit residential project at 970 Fellsway, covering design, traffic, and civil engineering peer reviews. This process concluded with the approval of a comprehensive permit and a partial linkage fee waiver based on off-site public improvements. Other large-scale 40B projects saw varying results, including the withdrawal of a 378-unit proposal at 280 Mystic Avenue and the approval of design refinements for a 350-unit development at 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway. Later, the board approved a lot split at 970 Fellsway to separate the new residential use from existing commercial structures.

threads.name: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Regulation
threads.summary: In 2026, the board began adjudicating petitions for accessory dwelling units under new state zoning regulations. Initial applications included a setback variance for an attached ADU on Fulton Street and attic expansions on Vassar and Wellesley Streets. The board has repeatedly continued hearings for these attic-based ADUs to seek legal counsel on how the state's new standards apply to specific architectural modifications like shed dormers. The board is currently awaiting modified designs that align with the board's interpretation of the updated guidelines.

threads.name: Residential Density and Two-Family Conversions
threads.summary: The board frequently reviews requests to convert single-family homes into two-family or multi-family dwellings to increase local housing density. While several conversions were approved on Pearl Street, Morton Avenue, and Main Street, others were denied when the applicant failed to demonstrate a statutory hardship. A notable case on Second Street required multiple continuances for the applicant to reduce building massing and height to meet neighborhood consistency concerns. Recent approvals have been conditioned on the use of permeable materials to manage the increased site drainage associated with higher density.

threads.name: Cannabis Business Licensing
threads.summary: The board managed the permitting process for cannabis-related commerce at 114 Mystic Avenue. In early 2026, the board approved special permits for medical cannabis sales and product manufacturing for Victory Gardens. A companion request for courier delivery services was initially continued to solicit feedback from the police chief and legal counsel. The delivery permit was eventually approved in July 2026.

threads.name: Environmental and Topographical Mitigations
threads.summary: Board decisions often address unique site conditions such as flooding and steep grades. The board granted a parking variance on Lincoln Street to allow the infilling of a below-grade garage that suffered from chronic flooding. Similarly, a variance was granted on Judkins Road for a garage addition to resolve drainage issues caused by the property's pie-shaped lot and topography. The board also approved a variance for a driveway on Ramstead Road on the condition that the previous apron be replaced with green space to improve site permeability.

threads.name: Board Administration and Leadership
threads.summary: The board's leadership and procedures underwent several changes between 2023 and 2026. Jamie Thompson was elected chair in April 2024, though previous chair Mike Caldera continued to lead specific ongoing hearings for procedural consistency. Following Thompson's resignation in early 2025, Caldera was re-elected as chair. During this time, the board also initiated a subcommittee to update its dated rules and regulations and explored AI software to address a backlog of meeting minutes.

periods.narrative: The board focused on major mixed-use amendments on Boston Avenue and the introduction of the large-scale 970 Fellsway Chapter 40B project.
This period was dominated by intensive design and traffic reviews for the 970 Fellsway development and the subsequent approval of its comprehensive permit.
The board's work shifted toward cannabis dispensary operations and navigating new state-mandated accessory dwelling unit regulations.
